hlni.insight: A short illustrative activity reveals where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
hlni.audienceGap: Students feel overwhelmed by degree choices without knowing what they actually want to practice.
hlni.viewerChange: Use a momentary sticking point to generate a productive inquiry.
hlni.support: The observation belongs to this activity; it supports a specific inquiry rather than a general degree choice.
hlni.payoff: The student uses the sticking point to formulate a concrete question for academic guidance.

reelTitle: B.Com vs BBA: Finding Your Focus
creativeAngle: Using a personal sticking point to frame a meaningful question
objective: To help students move past the B.Com vs BBA label by identifying their specific area of curiosity
targetAudience: +2 students seeking accessible, supportive guidance, including students worried about marks, confidence, or belonging

shots.name: The Overwhelmed Student
shots.visual: Student sitting at a desk with two notebooks labeled B.Com and BBA, looking confused at a prompt.
shots.dialogue: Stuck between B.Com and BBA? Don't let the labels stop you.
shots.cameraPerformance: Close-up on the student's frustrated expression.

shots.name: The Logic Puzzle
shots.visual: A notepad displays a simple logic puzzle. Student points to a specific step.
shots.dialogue: Try this: Task: Allocate 5 units across 3 departments. Why does that rule exist?
shots.cameraPerformance: Camera zooms in on the notepad task.

shots.name: The Meaningful Question
shots.visual: Student writes a question in their journal and looks at the camera with clarity.
shots.dialogue: Instead of choosing a degree, ask: Can you explain the logic behind these allocation rules? That's your next step.
shots.onscreenText: Can you explain the logic behind these allocation rules?

productionNotes.camera: Handheld feel to emphasize the student's personal process
productionNotes.editing: Rhythmic cuts on the task discovery

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Shifting the student from comparing degree titles to identifying the actual logic they find interesting through a practical task.

selected.title: The Sticking Point Journal
selected.audienceGap: Students feel overwhelmed by degree choices without knowing what they actually want to practice.
selected.hlni: A short illustrative activity can reveal where you need help or what you want to investigate next; it cannot determine which degree suits you.
selected.viewerChange: Use a momentary sticking point to generate a productive inquiry.
selected.concept: A student working through a sample problem identifies a specific point where they need clarification.
selected.device: A handheld notepad capturing a student's live reaction to a task.
selected.support: The observation belongs to this activity and participant; it supports a next question rather than a general prediction.
methodSteps: Try or inspect a clearly illustrative task.
Record one point where you needed help and one question you want to investigate.
Turn the observation into a question for a real course brief or course team.
selected.interpretationRule: Use the recorded observation to choose the next question, not to select a degree from one activity.
selected.visibleProof: A person records a specific sticking point and asks a different, more useful question afterward.
selected.payoff: Use the recorded observation to choose the next question, not to select a degree from one activity.
selected.limitations: A brief exercise does not measure aptitude, learning style, long-term interest or academic performance.

demonstration.input: A short logic puzzle regarding resource allocation.
demonstration.observation: The student records they are stuck on the 'why' behind the allocation rule.
demonstration.nextQuestion: Can you explain the logic behind these allocation rules?

comparedWith.hlni: A task label alone does not tell you what you must produce, what will be assessed, or what feedback you receive. Ask these as separate questions.
comparedWith.device: A split-screen view: one side shows a vague task, the other shows the three-column audit grid.
